slides.title: Describing Movement
slides.content:
1. Verbs of Change

Don't just say "go up" or "go down". Use professional verbs:

📈 UP: Increase, Rise, Grow, Soar (fly high), Skyrocket (go up very fast).
📉 DOWN: Decrease, Fall, Drop, Plummet (fall very fast), Crash.

Other movements: Fluctuate (up and down), Stabilize (stay the same), Peak (reach the top).

2. Adverbs (How fast?)

  • Dramatically / Sharply: Very fast change.
  • Steadily / Gradually: Slow, constant change.
  • Slightly: A very small change.
slides.speech_text: To sound professional when analyzing data, avoid simple words. Instead of 'it went up a lot', say 'sales skyrocketed'. Instead of 'it went down a little', say 'it decreased slightly'.

slides.title: Quarterly Sales Report
slides.content: Listen to the analyst describing the Q2 performance.
slides.audio_script:
Analyst: Let's look at the chart. In January, sales started at $10,000.
        Manager: And what happened in February?
        Analyst: In February, they rose steadily to $12,000. However, in March, we had a problem with the server, so sales plummeted to $5,000.
        Manager: That looks bad. Did we recover?
        Analyst: Yes. In April, after the fix, sales recovered dramatically, reaching a peak of $15,000.

quiz.question: How did sales recover in April?

slides.title: Prepositions: By vs To
slides.instruction: Select the correct preposition. This is tricky!

questions.explanation: BY indica la diferencia (el cambio). TO indica el número final.
El resultado final es $50, así que usamos TO.

questions.text: There was a sharp increase _____ demand.
questions.explanation: Decimos 'an increase IN something' (increase in sales, in demand, in price).

slides.title: Roleplay: Explain the Graph
slides.system_prompt:
You are a Board Director asking about company performance.
        The user is the Data Analyst.
        
        Steps:
        1. Ask: "How did our stocks perform last month?"
        2. Wait for the user to describe a movement (e.g., "They increased...").
        3. Ask for details: "Was it a sharp increase or a slight one?"
        4. Ask for numbers: "What number did we finish at?"
        
        Correction Focus: Ensure they use professional verbs (increase, drop, rise) instead of "go up/down".
slides.initial_message: I'm looking at the monthly report. Can you summarize how our stocks performed last month?
slides.user_goal: Describe a trend using a verb (e.g., increased) and an adverb (e.g., sharply).
